body:
Part of #114; split out under the reopening comment's instruction to ship all requirements or create linked follow-ups. Current profile migration still targets Chromium; PR #116 adds Safari cookies to that existing path.

Implement opt-in import into every controlled engine with the same JS/Rust/Python and CLI/command-stream options:

- Firefox cookies through cookies.sqlite/BiDi or the existing path without CDP; places.sqlite translation; logins.json + key4.db encryption; prefs.js and signed extensions where accepted.
- Playwright WebKit cookies through context.addCookies and localStorage/IndexedDB via storage state; persist supported files and explicitly report unsupported data classes.
- Same-engine full clone: snapshot the whole locked Chromium/Firefox profile (and Safari to controlled WebKit only where the formats are compatible), copy all supported stores, re-key encrypted stores, and exclude runtime lock files without silently discarding user data.
- Validate source and target options before mutating a target. A fresh profile remains the default and import remains opt-in.
- Keep existing Chromium features working; preserve domain filtering and per-source/target migrated/skipped/warnings reports.

Acceptance: fixture round trips into Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; actual browser acceptance tests for each available runtime; no accidental Chromium files in Firefox/WebKit profiles; encrypted-store tests; locked-profile snapshots; CLI command-stream tests; native parity in all three languages. Coordinate the shared generated source × target × data-class matrix and CI enforcement with #114's parity follow-up.
title: Import into Firefox and WebKit and support same-engine full profile clones (#114)
